name: Museo del Prado

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13046997 (centroid of the outline of the Villanueva building; long axis at 170.5°)

rights.note: Villanueva's building (1785–1819, finished by López Aguado) is what is modelled. Later works inside the same outline, kept only as plain massing: apse by Narciso Pascual y Colomer (1853, died 1870), north front by Francisco Jareño (1880s, died 1892), eastern ranges by Fernando Arbós (1911–1921, died 1916) and by Fernando Chueca Goitia and Manuel Lorente (1954–1956; Chueca died 2004), the Goya stair by Pedro Muguruza (1943–1946, died 1952). The last two are recent enough to be protected; they appear only as generic volumes (plain saw-tooth roofs, a plain stair). Rafael Moneo's 2007 extension (the Jerónimos building) is a separate OpenStreetMap building and is not included.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q160112_museo_del_prado.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The Villanueva building only (OSM relation 13046997); Moneo's Jerónimos extension is a separate building and is left out, and so are the Velázquez and Goya statues (their own OSM/Wikidata items). Outline, portico, apse, rotunda and Goya blocks from OpenStreetMap; roof layout from the PNOA orthophoto; heights measured on photos (±5 %): ground storey 6.4 m, Ionic loggia 6.9–11.9 m, cornice 14.8 m, Doric portico columns 10 m, attic 18.4 m. West front: six Doric columns, Barba's relief (stylised figures), arched openings with grilles alternating with niches (statues, vases) and portrait medallions on brick, the Ionic colonnade in front of the recessed upper wall, frieze windows, modillion cornice. North (Goya): podium with two stairs, two Ionic columns in antis, taller brick blocks. South (Murillo): door and a loggia of six Corinthian columns. Simplified/uncertain: one cornice height for the whole building, low hipped roofs with glass lanterns standing for the real skylights, generic windows on the brick ends and the east side, the interior plan, the number of bays (17 per gallery). y = 0 is the level of the Paseo del Prado front; the ground rises towards the east, so the foundations go 5 m down. The footprint is the OSM outline grown by 1 m (the convex hull would clear the gardens in front of the galleries and the neighbouring buildings to the east).
